Counsel for Respondent :- G.A.
Hon'ble Vinod Diwakar,J.

1. Heard learned counsel for the petitioner, learned AGA for the State-respondents and perused the record.
2.

The instant writ petition has been filed seeking quashing of the order dated 13.08.2024 passed by Additional Sessions Judge/Fast Track Court-I, District Gautambudh Nagar in Criminal Revision o.
506 of 2023 (Vishal Maheshwari Vs. State of U.P. and another) under Section 397 Cr.P.C, filed against the order dated 08.08.2023 passed by Civil Judge (Junior Division)/Fast Track Court-II,
Gautmbudh Nagar in Case No. 1085 of 2011 (State Vs. Vishal Maheshwari) arising out of Case Crime No. 17 of 2011, Under Section 498A, 323, 506 IPC and Section 3/4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act,
Police Station Mahila Thana, District Gautambudh Nagar.
3.

entities.text: Additional Sessions Judge/Fast Track Court-I, District Gautambudh Nagar
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the petitioner states that the learned Trial Court has not considered the fact that the present case is the case of no injury.
During investigation, no evidence with respect to the commission of alleged offence under Section 498A has been collected by the Investigating Officer.

The matter initially was settled between the husband and wife but subsequently could not acted Vishal Maheshwari vs State Of U.P. And Another on 9 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/37669460/

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the petitioner further submits that after four months of the date of the incident, First Information Report was registered without recording sufficient cause of delay in registration of FIR.
These facts have not been considered by the trial court while framing charge under Section 498A IPC.
The petitioner has moved an application under Section 239 Cr.P.C. for discharge but the same was erroneously rejected vide order dated 08.08.2023.

Aggrieved by order dated 08.08.2023, petitioner preferred the Criminal Revision No. 506 off 2023 before the Additional Sessions Judge/FTC-I, District Gautambudh Nagar, which too was rejected, hence the instant writ petition has been filed challenging the impugned orders.

entities.text: Additional Sessions Judge/FTC-I, District Gautambudh Nagar
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 4. Per contra, learned AGA vehemently opposed the contentions raised on behalf of the petitioner and submits that the impugned orders passed by the Trial Court have been passed in accordance with law and do not warrant any interference by this Court.

5. The applicant has filed an application under Section 239 of the Code of Criminal Procedure alleging that on 01.02.2011, no such incident as alleged by the prosecution has ever taken place with the victim.

The learned Trial Court after evaluating the evidence available before it, came to the conclusion that an incident of marpeet took place with the victim on 01.02.2011 and further the accused-applicant has made additional demand of dowry and on account of non fulfillment of the same, she was subjected to cruelty, hence the trial court vide order dated 08.08.2023 rejected the discharge application of the applicant.
6.

Aggrieved by order dated 08.08.2023, the accused-applicant has preferred Criminal Revision No.
506 of 2023 before the Revisional Court, which too was rejected vide order dated 13.08.2024, on the ground that prima facie a case for committing cruelty with the victim and demand of dowry is made out.

In such circumstances, this Court is of the view that the orders impugned passed by the Trial Court do not warrant any interference in the writ jurisdiction under Article 227 of the Constitution of India.
7. Accordingly, the writ petition is dismissed.
Order Date :- 9.4.2025 Prajapati Justice Vinod Diwakar  Vishal Maheshwari vs State Of U.P.
